claim: A model that only proposes steps, with code-owned best-first search and an exact checker, beat prior non-neural provers by a large margin (Metamath 56.22% vs 21.16%).
agent_test: Same task set: frozen LLM proposes k next steps, code keeps a goal queue ranked by a program score, versus one long free-form attempt; equal total tokens.

claim: More checked attempts keep helping with shrinking returns: GPT-f gains +4.39, +3.97, +2.99, +2.45 points per doubling of attempts (a=4..32); BFS-Prover goes 64.98% at pass@64 to 70.83% at pass@2048 (about log scaling).
agent_test: Plot solve rate against attempts (2,4,8,16,32) at a fixed token total and check for the same diminishing shape.

claim: At fixed compute, many samples from a smaller model beat fewer from a larger one (774M with many attempts), and size gains saturate (700M to 1.5B no gain).
agent_test: Compare one deep pass of a strong model against several cheap passes at equal tokens.

claim: A value or score over partial states helps: GPT-f policy+value 47.21% vs policy-only 43.15% at iteration 2 (not 42.56%; see critique); HTPS value-guided search lifted Metamath held-out from 56.5% (GPT-f) to 65.4%. Open: BFS-Prover (no value head, length-normalised model log-prob score) reaches 70.83% at 2048x2x600, but no paper compares a code-computed state score with a learned value head.
agent_test: Rank open goals by a code-computed score (open-goal count, proof size) versus model self-rating, at equal tokens.

claim: Search that tracks AND-OR subgoal structure (all children must be solved) is needed because one tactic can create several subgoals; AlphaProof also uses AND-OR trees.
agent_test: Track subgoal sets in code and compare with flat retry on multi-lemma problems.

claim: Tool handoff gives large gains: Thor 39.0% to 57.0% on PISA with 8.2% solved by neither part alone; removing the automated prover from DSP costs 9.8 points (valid) and 9.0 (test). The baseline for Thor is a union of independent runs (48.8%), not a fixed 'call the solver at each goal' rule; interleaving adds 8.2 points over the union.
agent_test: Let the model decide when to call a solver or checker versus doing every step in text; equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Premise handling is a bottleneck: Thor model-chosen premise steps advance a proof 1.9% of the time vs 28.2% without premises (observational); removing proof context costs 3.4 points (57.0 to 53.6); code retrieval raised ReProver 47.6 to 51.2.
agent_test: Give the agent code-retrieved lemmas versus a long list in context; measure solve rate.

claim: Informal draft then formal fill (DSP) doubled Isabelle miniF2F-test success (20.9% to 39.3%), and model-written informal proofs were close to human ones. DSP+ (Lean 4, training-free) replicates the pipeline (miniF2F-test 79.5% at 1024 attempts) but finds the draft adds little with a strong executor: pass@128 none 71.7%, GPT-4o 71.7%, QwQ 74.2%, R1 75.8%, and human informal proofs gave no overall gain.
agent_test: Draft a plan in language, then fill each gap by checked sub-calls; compare with a direct attempt.

claim: A scaffold multiplies the proposer, it does not replace it: COPRA GPT-4 26.63% vs GPT-3.5 9.02% and CodeLlama 5.73%; Hilbert on PutnamBench with one attempt per problem 55.9% (Gemini 2.5 Pro) vs 13.3% (gpt-oss-120b) with the same loop and prover; raw GPT-4 on PutnamBench 2024 1/640. On medium-difficulty sets (miniF2F) the same loop lifts even weaker planners to 90%+. No clean sweep of raw pass rate has been run, so the floor is not isolated.
agent_test: Measure raw pass rate of our model first; add the loop only above a floor. One paper, one benchmark: replicate.

claim: Feeding checker errors and history back with backtracking helps: COPRA 24.59% without backtracking vs 26.63% with; 60 independent samples with no state feedback reach only 15.98%.
agent_test: Ablate checker feedback and backtracking at equal query count.

claim: Informal hints and extra queries add under one point in COPRA (29.09 to 29.92 to 30.74) on 244 items, within noise.
agent_test: Do not rely on such small ablation gaps; use more items.

claim: Random splits overstate prover performance: LeanDojo novel_premises drops ReProver 51.2 to 26.3 and GPT-4 29.0 to 7.4, so memorization and leakage inflate results.
agent_test: Report a novel held-out split for our agent tests and check contamination.

claim: Whole-proof sampling is competitive with stepwise tree search: for DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 at 32x6400 samples, single pass is 60.2% and RMaxTS 62.7% (63.5% in the best mix), a gain of 2.5 to 3.3 points; plain UCT without intrinsic reward falls to the non-search level. Budgets are around 200k samples.
agent_test: At equal total samples compare parallel independent attempts with a tree reusing prefixes.

claim: Truncate-and-resume (keep the verified prefix, regenerate from the last good state) is a concrete operator; code-only resume without tactic-state information does worse.
agent_test: Keep the verified prefix of a failed attempt versus restarting; equal tokens.

claim: Verified self-generated data with an exact checker scales: expert iteration raised mathlib pass@1 56.3 to 62.6 over 9 iterations and solved problems sampling alone never reached; DeepSeek-Prover, Goedel and STP extend this.
agent_test: Not testable without training; frozen analogue is keeping verified lemmas in context.

claim: Decomposition into lemma subgoals, solved separately and stitched, is the strongest recent recipe: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 88.9% miniF2F, 47/658 Putnam; Seed-Prover 99.6% miniF2F, 331/657 Putnam. Frozen-model versions work too: Hilbert (general reasoner + trained prover, code loop) 99.2% miniF2F and 462/660 Putnam; LEGO-Prover (frozen GPT-3.5) 50.0% test vs 39.3% for Thor; recursion depth 2 gives 98.36% vs about 75% with no decomposition. None of these is an equal-token comparison.
agent_test: Compare a decomposed-lemma loop with a monolithic attempt on multi-step problems at equal tokens.

claim: Checker-feedback refinement helps but is budget-confounded: Seed-Prover light 8-16 refinements matches pass@64-256; Goedel-Prover-V2 self-correction 88.1 to 90.4 on miniF2F used 40k vs 30k tokens. New: Seed-Prover's light-setting claim has no matched ablation (one IMO 2022 P2 anecdote); a 2026 controlled study (Qwen3.6-27B, DS-Prover-V2-7B, 11 hard problems, 64 attempts) found no feedback condition beat instruction-only resampling and that showing the failed proof lowers success through copying.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of refine-on-error against fresh resampling.

claim: Extra search and test-time compute keeps paying on hard problems: AlphaProof formal-imo 33.2/43.7/53.9/58.3 and PutnamBench 27.9/39.4/45.5/56.1 from 2 TPU-min to 500 TPU-days (the last steps use test-time RL, which changes weights).
agent_test: Frozen analogue: solve easier variants first and keep them as context.

claim: An informal LLM-verifier loop solved 5 of 6 IMO 2025 problems with three different models vs 21.4-38.1% for best-of-32; the verifier is an LLM with no measured error rate, and the result is from the authors' own pipeline. Verifier error rates are now measured elsewhere: see K25.
agent_test: Verify-and-revise with an independent verifier vs best-of-N at equal tokens; measure verifier false-pass rate.

claim: A formal checker passes the statement given, not the intended problem: Goedel-Prover had a Putnam solve withdrawn for mis-formalization, and two GPT-f curriculum IMO solves are weakened versions. Benchmark statements are also wrong: DSP+ found 8 mis-formalised miniF2F statements; an autoformalisation scored 97% by auto-check and 67% by a Lean expert.
agent_test: Add a check that the verified statement equals the original question.

claim: Guess many candidate answers, refute wrong ones with a checker, then prove the survivor (AlphaProof at IMO 2024: 28/42 with AlphaGeometry 2, 2-3 days per solved problem).
agent_test: Generate candidates, test by code, prove the survivor; equal tokens vs single answer.

claim: Checker-format tuning matters: Kimina-Prover reaches 68.85% pass@32 and 80.7% at pass@8192 on miniF2F, while Gemini scores 37.70% and o3 24.59% in the same table.
agent_test: Test our model on the checker output format before comparing arms.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Benchmarks saturate: miniF2F-test went from 29.6% (2022) to 99.6% (2025), while PutnamBench stays hard (7% to 50% by system and budget).
agent_test: Use unsaturated items for our tests.

claim: Headline numbers depend on budget: DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL gets 51.6% at 128 samples but 60.2% only at 32x6400 samples; cumulative pass rates (HTPS 82.6% Metamath valid) include training on valid statements.
agent_test: State attempts per item for every arm.

claim: LLM verifiers of natural-language proofs are too lenient to be a final gate: QEDBench (272 problems) human pass 67.7%, judges 72 to 90%, false-pass (leniency) rates 38.0% (GPT-5.2 Pro), 39.6% (DeepSeek-V3), 74.8% (Llama 4 Maverick); GPT-5 judged 7 of 48 flawed USAMO proofs correct even with a reference solution or 5 votes; olympiad judges reach 77 to 88% balanced accuracy, prompt changes move accuracy by up to 27 points, and small judges are up to 25 points less self-consistent. Cheap shortcuts (an MLP on embeddings 75.3%, a keyword rule 65.1%) rival mid judges on one benchmark.
agent_test: Where no exact checker exists, run the LLM verifier on known-wrong proofs from our own tasks and report the false-pass rate; accept only on agreement across several differently prompted judgements, and never as the final gate if the false-pass rate exceeds a stated limit.

claim: With a strong executor the informal plan text adds little: DSP+ pass@128 without a draft 71.7% vs 71.7% (GPT-4o), 73.0% (V3), 74.2% (QwQ), 75.8% (R1); the prover choice matters more (BFS-Prover 74.2% vs common tactics 47.5%), and sketch fixes (hypothesis specification, masking error lines) cause a significant drop when removed.
agent_test: Run the subgoal-fill loop with and without a written plan on the same tasks at equal tokens; keep the plan only if it pays for its tokens.

claim: Contamination of miniF2F and PutnamBench in frontier LLMs is warned about but not measured in any paper found: PutnamBench argues formal statements are new yet informal solutions are public; a 2026 prover paper reports decontamination (snippet only); PutnamBench results moved from about 0.2% (GPT-4, 2024) to 70% (2025).
agent_test: Build the test set from items newer than the model cutoff or freshly restated, and keep a restated-twin control for each old item.

claim: Recursive decomposition has fast diminishing returns by depth: Hilbert miniF2F 98.36% at D=2 and 98.7% at D=3 against about 75% with no decomposition; retrieval of library facts adds 1.3 points and cuts reasoner tokens from 4.0M to 2.3M (Goedel case).
agent_test: Cap decomposition depth at 2 or 3 in the schema and compare to depth 4 or more.

claim: A frozen model with a lemma library plus a checker gains from reuse: LEGO-Prover (GPT-3.5, no training) valid 50.4% with the growing skill library vs 47.1% without at 50 attempts (+3.3 points); 24% of its valid proofs used retrieved skills.
agent_test: Keep checked lemmas in a store the agent can retrieve from across subtasks; measure solves with and without it at equal tokens.
